global_sound:
ONE SHARED SOUND WORLD, v2 "contemporary pop-musical": a modern stage-and-screen pop-musical hybrid. A polished pop band (punchy tight kick and snare, pop piano with bright octave hooks, electric and acoustic guitars, synth pads and plucks, sub bass, handclaps and stomps) sits ON a cinematic orchestra (sweeping strings, horns, harp, glockenspiel, timpani for climaxes). Lead vocals are upfront and conversational in the verses, with modern pop-belt mix climaxes. Stacked harmonies, doubled hooks and short ad-libs ("ooh", "mm-hm", "hey!") come in the choruses, and a gang-vocal ensemble chants the hooks. Crisp British English diction throughout, contemporary and witty, never twee. Every song uses verse / pre-chorus / big repeating chorus / bridge / final chorus, and most land a key change in the last chorus (Songs 1, 7 and 8 deliberately don't). Every song still opens with a SUNG time stamp.

THREE RECURRING SONIC SIGNATURES, modernised. Name them in the style of every relevant song.
(1) GLIDE: a rising harp-and-synth shimmer swell that resolves into a smooth soaring legato string line. It plays whenever the tendon moves well.
(2) SCARLETT: a sliding sub-bass, a muted trumpet, finger snaps and a swung electro-swing hi-hat. It plays whenever she lurks.
(3) TAP: a crisp double tick of rimshot and glockenspiel, for Digby, Tinel's taps and every rep count.

VOICES FROM ABOVE (Mae, Wren, Teo, and Thea when she speaks) are dry and close-miked with no reverb, like a phone voice note, against the big wet reverb of the kingdom. Every plot-critical spoken line is also carried in a sung lyric.

GENRE MAP (each song different):
1. Pop-orchestral ensemble opener with a ticking-clock groove.
2. Intimate piano-pop power ballad.
3. Comic chamber-pop patter trio.
4. Acoustic-pop love duet in 6/8.
5. Bubblegum cheer-pop ensemble with a girl-group Greek chorus.
6. Pop-rock act-one-finale anthem.
7. Slinky dark electro-swing villain number.
8. Country-pop road-trip song with a whistle hook.
9. Gospel and R&B-pop eleven-o'clock ballad.
10. Stomp-clap orchestral pop finale that reprises Song 1's hook.

STYLE PROMPT RULES: each style prompt is production DNA plus the verbatim voice identities, under 1000 characters. Never name an artist, composer, studio, film, song, show or musical.

LYRIC RULES:
- Every line is original.
- Avoid famous musical phrases: "let it go", "defying gravity", "popular", "omigod", "you guys", "for good", "bend and snap".
- The bible's "Place and hold, and then let go." is sung only as the whole line. Never echo or repeat "let go" on its own.
- Never pair the words "bend" and "snap" in a single line. Teo's "Stuck, not snapped" and Prox's "That's how a stuck thing snaps" stay as they are, in Song 9 only, away from any cheer section.
- No "believe", "fly", "rise", "free", "I've learned" and no direct address to the audience.
- Every belt sits on a concrete action: a count, a stitch, a stair, a fist, a shoelace.
- A joke undercuts every swell.
- Only Scarlett says "darling". Thea says "my love" and "lovely".

songs.title: Got It in Hand
songs.modern_archetype: Contemporary pop-musical opening number: a high-energy 'this is our world' ensemble showcase that builds and builds, then hits a dead stop on the inciting incident
songs.production_dna: Upbeat pop-orchestral opening ensemble number, 124 BPM 4/4, ticking-clock hi-hat and staccato pop-piano pulse, punchy kick, handclaps, driving strings, bright horns, glockenspiel, synth pads, big gang-vocal chorus, stacked harmonies. GLIDE: rising harp-and-synth shimmer swell into soaring legato strings. Swaggering low brass and kick for the king. Dry close-miked voices from above with no reverb, like a phone voice note. Thinning to a lone tick, a sudden dead stop and silence, tense string tremolo, an unresolved synth-pad and string chord. Crisp British English diction. Voices: ENSEMBLE, PROX and TIP in unison, KING, PULLEYS, LUMBO and DIGBY cameos, MAE and WREN from above.
songs.structure:
No key change: the energy rises all the way into the stop.

[Intro | ENSEMBLE, ticking clock and piano] Sung time stamp, exact: 'A Tuesday in October, a quarter to eight, / in the left hand of Doctor Mae.'

[Verse 1 | ENSEMBLE] The holding hand's inventory, fast and conversational: coffee, phone, wheel, Wren across the road. It has mended a thousand hands.

[Pre-Chorus | ENSEMBLE, building] 'She says "Make a fist for me. Now open." / to a thousand hands.' A band stab hits on 'fist' and a shimmer opens on 'open'.

[Chorus | ENSEMBLE gang vocals, handclaps] The HOOK.

[Verse 2 | KING, rock swagger] Eight bars only: 'I PULL, and the fingers close', three daughters on one muscle.

[Post-Chorus | ENSEMBLE chant] 'Prox-an-tip! Prox-an-tip! / So long together they forgot that they were two!'

[Hook 2 | PROX and TIP in unison, GLIDE] The ONE LINE couplet, EXACT, first time.

[Cameo Round | quickfire, one line each over stop-time hits] ENSEMBLE: 'Big Sister splits and hugs her from beneath.' PULLEYS: 'We hold her to the bone, or else she'd bowstring!' LUMBO: 'Nobody knows what I do!' DIGBY: 'Ulnar side. I feel everything.'

[Chorus 2 | ENSEMBLE, then PROX and TIP in unison] The HOOK, then the ONE LINE couplet EXACT, second time.

[Verse 3 | ENSEMBLE, bragging chant] 'never the avocado, / never the bagel in your palm!'

[Break | MAE and WREN from Above, dry] MAE: 'Wren, hold still! Sun cream! Shoes on!' WREN: 'I can cut it!' MAE: 'Knives are sharp. Give it here, you'll be late.'

[Build | ENSEMBLE hushed, music thinning to the tick] The action is sung so it carries without the spoken lines: 'and she holds the bagel in her palm, / the ring finger curled around...' Ghost echo: '(got it in hand... got it in hand...)'.

[Final Chorus | PROX and TIP in unison, bright and unaware] 'one line from the elbow to the-' and the music cuts off.

[Stop | silence]

[Break | string tremolo] PROX: 'Tip?' TIP: 'Prox?'

[Break | KING roar, low brass] 'Come home! Come home!'

[Verse 4 | ENSEMBLE, falling strings] The King drags her to the palm, and as Mae opens her hand Tip slides away down to the end of the world.

[Break | DIGBY] 'Half of me's gone quiet.'

[Break | MAE, half-sung through her teeth] 'Look at the cascade. / Hold the middle joint. Bend the tip. / ...Nothing.'

[Break | ENSEMBLE, brass stabs] 'Zone Two! No Man's Land!'

[Outro | MAE] 'Of course it's Zone Two.' Unresolved chord.
songs.hook_idea: A pun chant with built-in dramatic irony: 'We've got it in hand! (Got it in hand!) / The coffee, the keys, the phone and Wren, / we've got it in hand! (Hey!)'. The kingdom boasts that it has everything under control, seconds before Mae loses control of the knife. The irony is never remarked on. The hook returns in Song 10, flipped, as a small hand slips out of the big one. The bible's chant 'We're the holding hand!' becomes the answering half-line under it.
songs.keep_from_v1:
- The exact sung time stamp.
- The holding-hand inventory.
- 'never the avocado, / never the bagel in your palm!' as the brag chant.
- The Mae, Wren and bagel exchange, verbatim.
- 'and she holds the bagel in her palm, / the ring finger curled around'.
- The ONE LINE couplet twice in full and cut off the third time.
- The one-line cameos: 'We hold her to the bone, or else she'd bowstring!', 'Nobody knows what I do!' and 'Ulnar side. I feel everything.'
- 'Half of me's gone quiet.'
- Mae's cascade self-test.
- 'Of course it's Zone Two.'

songs.title: The Space Between
songs.modern_archetype: Intimate piano-pop power ballad as the heroine's I-want song, with a comic sidekick who keeps interrupting her big moment
songs.production_dna: Intimate piano-pop power ballad, 74 BPM, solo felt piano and soft synth pad intro, conversational breathy mezzo verses, half-time drums and sub bass entering at the first chorus, warm strings swelling, stacked harmonies on the hook, quick comic patter breaks over pizzicato strings and a glitchy tick beat for a nervous tenor, distant father's line on low brass and timpani, a wistful GLIDE fragment (harp-and-synth shimmer that fades), one dry close-miked spoken line from above, big key change into a soaring sustained chest belt, open ending on a sustained piano chord. British English diction.
songs.structure:
Key change: LUMBO's 'Day two!' kicks it straight into the final chorus.

[Intro | PROX, felt piano] Time stamp: 'Day nought, the dark of the palm, / the finger in a bandage, and Mae can't sleep.'

[Verse 1 | PROX, conversational and wry] She introduces herself in modern diction, half of a name. She lands one dry joke about being hauled up the arm 'like a blind on a string'.

[Spoken | LUMBO] 'Ahem. Down here. Lumbo.' He held on, which is why she stopped in the palm.

[Interlude | KING, distant] 'Prox! Come home!'

[Patter | LUMBO, rapid] The lumbrical-plus gag: 'Sorry! Sorry! That's me! Lumbrical plus! / Nobody knows what I do, / and NOW they do!'

[Spoken | MAE from Above] 'Paradoxical extension. Lovely.'

[Verse 2 | PROX] The Proxantip back-story: married since before Mae learned to crawl. Tip has never moved by himself.

[Pre-Chorus | PROX, fragile, GLIDE fragment] The ONE LINE couplet with its last word missing: 'Through the sheath and past the pulleys, / one line from the elbow to the...'

[Chorus | PROX, belt-mix, drums in] The SPACE couplet EXACT, then 'the longest inch I've ever seen', then the couplet again.

[Post-Chorus | PROX, stacked harmonies] The tag hook.

[Spoken | LUMBO] 'Nearer three centimetres, technically.'

[Verse 3 | PROX, resolve building] 'back down the tunnel, past the rings, through No Man's Land'.

[Bridge | KING, low brass] 'Come home, stay where it's safe.'

[Bridge Answer | PROX, no drums] 'You pulled me here, Papa. / You can't pull me home.'

[Spoken | LUMBO] 'The surgeon comes on Thursday! Day two!'

[Key Change | PROX belt] 'Day two!'

[Final Chorus | PROX, big sustained belt, full band and strings] The SPACE couplet EXACT, then 'Wait for me, Tip... I'm coming down through No Man's Land.'

[Outro | LUMBO] 'I'll come too. Technically I have to. I'm attached.'

[End | PROX whisper] 'Day two.'
songs.hook_idea: The chorus is the SPACE couplet sung EXACTLY ('I never knew that we were two / until there was a space between.'). A short original post-chorus earworm comes after it, a falling three-note 'We were two. (Ooh.) / We were two, / and I never even counted.' The counting joke is a deliberate seed for the counting in Songs 5, 6 and 9.
songs.keep_from_v1:
- The time stamp.
- Lumbo's 'I held on! Nobody ever thanks the lumbrical!'
- The full lumbrical-plus patter and 'Sorry! Sorry! That's me!'
- Mae's 'Paradoxical extension. Lovely.'
- 'the longest inch I've ever seen', answered by 'Nearer three centimetres, technically.'
- The King's 'Come home, stay where it's safe.'
- 'You pulled me here, Papa. / You can't pull me home.'
- 'Day two!' as the key-change trigger.
- 'Lumbo always comes. Technically I have to. I'm attached.'

songs.title: Vent Me Not
songs.modern_archetype: Comic patter-pop trio (the modern musical-comedy 'rapid-fire gossip' number), with a spooky trap-door drop into the villain's sound
songs.production_dna: Comic chamber-pop patter number, 150 BPM, frantic staccato strings, plucky pizzicato and harpsichord-like synth pluck, tick-tock woodblock, stomp-clap backbeat, piccolo flourishes, rapid tongue-twister patter traded between two grand posh wobbling operatic sopranos and a dry deadpan alto, a charming boyish tenor verse, a sudden half-time spooky drop into the SCARLETT signature (sliding sub-bass, muted trumpet, finger snaps, swung hi-hat) under whispered voices, then a snap back to bright major, a half-step key lift for the last chorus, a big three-hit operatic button and a dry spoken tag. British English diction.
songs.structure:
Key change: a half-step lift into the last chorus.

[Intro | staccato strings]

[Verse 1 | PULLEYS] Time stamp: 'Day one, the finger tunnel, / and the pulleys cannot sleep!'

[Patter 1 | A2 and A4 trading lines] 'He may VENT us!', explained for the families as 'A little slit to let her through!' and the blame-passing begins.

[Break | A1, deadpan] 'Tuesday. Trigger finger. Local. Again. / At least it wasn't a rugby shirt.'

[Chorus | PULLEYS] The HOOK, then the rule refrain.

[Patter 2 | faster] The bowstring scandal: 'Lifting off the bone in PUBLIC! / Whatever would the knuckles say?'

[Break | A3 and A5] 'Nobody mentions us.'

[Verse 2 | TIP, swaggering pop tenor] 'Evening, ladies. Tip.' He mangles the ONE LINE couplet ('Through the sheath and past the- / (Us, dear. US.)'), then the vanity lines 'I'm the bit that touches EVERYTHING. / Phones. Noses. I've been in a bagel.' and '(That's how we got into this.)'

[Bridge | TIP, half-time falsetto] The honest confession: he has never moved by himself, and only bends when Prox pulls.

[Drop | A1 as spooky narrator, SCARLETT signature] 'On old Doctor Bunnell's map / they call it No Man's Land.' The name is sung clearly twice: 'Her name is Scarlett Adhesion. (Scarlett Adhesion!)' and 'She moves into any space that stops moving.' TIP: 'Then I'll just keep moving.' A1: 'You just said you can't.' TIP: '...Ah.'

[Final Chorus | full trio and TIP, half-step key lift] The HOOK plus the rule refrain plus 'let him thread her back beneath us'.

[Outro | operatic three-hit button] 'VENT... ME... NOT!', then A1: '(Vent A-four. She'll be fine.)', A4: 'How DARE you!', A3 and A5: '(Nobody mentions us.)'
songs.hook_idea: A blame-passing call-and-response hook that ping-pongs between the sopranos: 'Vent me not! (Vent HER!) / Not me, not me, / a sliver off of somebody else! / Vent me not!' It is paired with the patter rule-refrain as a second hook: 'A4, or a little of A2, my dear, / but NEVER both. We are not animals! (We are not animals!)'
songs.keep_from_v1:
- The time stamp.
- 'Oh, the horror! Oh, the scalpel!'
- 'A little slit in ME, my dear? Or a little slit in YOU?'
- A1's Tuesday trigger-finger line and the rugby shirt.
- The exact A4/A2 rule and 'We are not animals!'
- 'Lifting off the bone in PUBLIC!' and 'Whatever would the knuckles say?'
- 'Nobody mentions us.'
- Tip's vanity verse and '(That's how we got into this.)'
- The mangled ONE LINE couplet.
- The Bunnell's map interlude.
- 'You just said you can't. ...Ah.'
- The 'Vent A-four. She'll be fine.' / 'How DARE you!' button.

songs.title: Make It Six
songs.modern_archetype: Acoustic-pop love duet (the contemporary 'reunion' duet), with an operating-theatre spoken frame and a held-breath breakdown before the payoff
songs.production_dna: Tender acoustic-pop love duet in lilting 6/8, about 84 BPM, fingerpicked acoustic guitar and soft felt piano, a gentle heartbeat-like kick and a faint monitor-beep tick, calm close-miked half-spoken baritone and dry woman's voice from above with no reverb, mezzo and tenor trading conversational verses then locking into close pop harmony, cello and strings swelling, a held-breath breakdown with a sudden string catch and silence, GLIDE (harp-and-synth shimmer into soaring legato strings) on the release, full band and wordless choir, a key change into the last chorus, glowing chord, short soft coda. British English diction.
songs.structure:
Key change: after 'Oh. There it is.', the final chorus goes up a key with the ONE LINE couplet in harmony.

[Intro | guitar and monitor tick] '(ooh...)'

[Verse 1 | TEO, half-sung] Time stamp: 'Day two, the theatre lights, / and Mae is wide awake. / No tourniquet, no sleep, / just a needle of local and a steady hand.'

[Spoken | MAE and TEO] MAE: 'They cut my ring off in A and E.' TEO: 'Standard.'

[Verse 2 | TEO] 'I draw a lightning bolt...' MAE: 'Bigger.' TEO: 'Mae.'

[Verse 3 | PROX, wonder] The slim tube, '(Borrowed from the children's ward.)', and 'a needle pins me like a butterfly'.

[Spoken | TEO] 'Straighten the finger for me, Mae... There you are. You ran.'

[Verse 4 | TIP, cheeky] 'I didn't run, I slid!' Married since before she learned to crawl. PROX: 'Through No Man's Land, Tip. I said I would.'

[Pre-Chorus | spoken and sung exchange] MAE: 'Four strands, Teo.' TEO: 'Four's the minimum.' TIP: 'Make it six, if you love me.' TEO: 'Six, then.'

[Chorus | PROX and TIP in harmony] The counting-vow HOOK, then TEO: 'and a running stitch around the edge'.

[Verse 5 | PROX, then TIP] The SPACE couplet EXACT, bent to 'Now there's barely a space between, / three millimetres, never more.'

[Breakdown | held breath, pizzicato tick] TEO: 'Make a fist for me.' A string catch. PROX and TIP: 'We're caught on the edge of A-four!' PULLEYS: 'Only A-four! Spare the A-two!' TEO: 'Just a sliver.' TEO: 'Again. Make a fist for me.' MAE: 'I've said that to a thousand patients.' TEO: 'Then you know the next bit. / Now open.' One open harp arpeggio. MAE: 'Oh. There it is.'

[Final Chorus | key change, GLIDE, PROX and TIP] The ONE LINE couplet EXACT in two-part HARMONY, then the counting vows with 'gliding, gliding, down and back again', then the tag 'make it six'.

[Coda | TEO] 'And last, the little nerve, / with thread finer than a hair.' DIGBY: 'Cheers.' PROX and TIP: 'Home in plaster, hand held high.'
songs.hook_idea: A counting-vow chorus that people can sing back, with one strand per ordinary thing the hand holds: 'One for the morning, one for the dark, / one for the kettle, one for the car, / one for the phone, and one for Wren.' It ends on a cheeky original tag in Tip's falsetto, '(Make it six... make it six, if you love me)', so the title is the earworm.
songs.keep_from_v1:
- The time stamp and the WALANT lines.
- The ring cut off in A and E, and 'Standard.'
- The lightning bolt with 'Bigger.' / 'Mae.'
- The tube borrowed from the children's ward.
- The butterfly needle.
- 'There you are. You ran.' and 'I didn't run, I slid!'
- The four-strands / six-then exchange, verbatim.
- The counting vows.
- The SPACE couplet and its 'three millimetres, never more' bend.
- The full fist / A4 vent / 'Now open.' / 'Oh. There it is.' sequence.
- The nerve last, with 'Cheers.'
- 'Home in plaster, hand held high.'

songs.title: Thea's Rules
songs.modern_archetype: Peppy bubblegum cheer-pop ensemble number (the 'pep-rally girl-group' showstopper), with a girl-group Greek chorus of waiting-room patients and a serious half-time bridge
songs.production_dna: Peppy bubblegum cheer-pop ensemble showstopper, 138 BPM, bouncy synth bass, bright pop piano stabs, handclaps and stomps, marching-band snare and a coach's whistle, cheer chants and spelled-out shouts, a girl-group trio as Greek chorus in tight bright harmony, warm brassy soul-pop alto lead with laughing asides, dry close-miked woman's voice arguing from above, TAP (crisp double tick of rimshot and glockenspiel) on every rep count, a sparkling glockenspiel and synth shimmer for the splint magic, a half-time serious bridge with strings and soft piano, a key change into a stacked shout chorus, a cheeky stab-and-whistle button. British English diction.
songs.structure:
Key change: into the shout chorus, after Digby's tap.

[Intro | THEA, whistle and claps] Time stamp: 'Day three, the clinic, / and the water bath is warm.'

[Stop | band drops, THEA spoken] 'Stitched isn't healed, my love. / Stitched is day two. Healed is January.'

[Verse 1 | THEA] She sends up Song 4's romance, then the SPACE redefinition EXACT: 'the space between that matters now / is you and the tunnel wall, a drop of water wide.'

[Pre-Chorus | PROX and TIP] 'Not just together. Gliding.'

[Verse 2 | THEA, glockenspiel and synth shimmer] Off with the plaster and into the water bath. 'A pumpkin to a carriage, love!' Then 'A wall at your back, / and an open road ahead.', sung ONCE. The wand is a goniometer.

[Cheer Break | MAE, then the HANDS-UP GIRLS] MAE: 'Dorsal blocking splint. I make my juniors spell it.' THEA: 'Go on, then.' HANDS-UP GIRLS: 'D! O! R! S! A! L!'

[Chorus | THEA with the HANDS-UP GIRLS echoing] 'These are my rules! (Thea's rules!) / Move it early! (Move it early!)' THEA sings 'The good hand bends it down for you, / place and hold, and then let go.' as one whole line and the girls echo the WHOLE line. Then 'Straight inside the splint, my love, / but never, never past it!' and 'Every hour, ten of each.'

[Verse 3 | THEA and MAE, rapid-fire stop-time] THEA: 'Hand above your heart!' MAE: 'It's in a sling. It's fine.' The waiting-room joke, with HANDS-UP GIRLS: 'Ooh, ooh, Miss! Me, Miss!' THEA: 'Swelling is glue! (Swelling is glue!)' THEA: 'Smoke?' MAE: 'I'm a surgeon.' THEA: 'So are half my smokers.' MAE: 'I wrote the protocol!' THEA: 'I've read it. Ten more.' THEA: 'In here you're not the surgeon, my love. / You're the hand.' THEA: 'The operation took him forty minutes. / The next twelve weeks are mine.'

[Verse 4 | KING, flexing] 'I'll close that finger in one almighty heave!' THEA: 'Pull with a whisper, Your Majesty.' KING: 'A... whisper?' The girls echo the motif line.

[Bridge | half-time, THEA serious] Days five to twenty-one, mend from the inside, 'builders build every which way', 'Two ways to lose a tendon: / tear it, or glue it.' PROX: 'Tear it...' TIP: '...or glue it.'

[Break | TAP] THEA: 'Anyone down there?' DIGBY: 'Ma'am, I'm on my way.'

[Shout Chorus | key change, everyone] The HOOK stacked with 'Don't tear it! Don't glue it!' MAE: 'Fine. FINE. Every hour.' THEA: 'Lovely.'

[Outro | THEA] 'Ten more, my love. One... two...' TAP.
songs.hook_idea: A cheer-chant hook made of the actual rehab rules, built for a crowd to shout back: 'Little and often! (Little and often!) / Gentle and slow! (Gentle and slow!) / Hand up high, never past the wall, / these are the rules! (THEA'S RULES!)'. The spelled-out 'D! O! R! S! A! L!' cheer is the second earworm. Thea is never cutesy: the girls are bubblegum, and she is the brisk coach.
songs.keep_from_v1:
- The time stamp.
- 'Stitched isn't healed, my love.'
- The exact SPACE redefinition.
- 'Not just together. Gliding.'
- 'A pumpkin to a carriage'.
- The once-only 'A wall at your back' line.
- The goniometer wand.
- The DORSAL spelling gag.
- The waiting room full of hands up 'like they've got a question'.
- 'Swelling is glue!'
- 'So are half my smokers.'
- 'No more rubber bands, my love!'
- 'I wrote the protocol!' / 'I've read it. Ten more.'
- 'You're the hand.'
- 'Forty minutes / next twelve weeks are mine'.
- 'Pull with a whisper, Your Majesty.' / 'A... whisper?'
- 'Tear it, or glue it.'
- 'Ma'am, I'm on my way.'
- 'Lovely.'

songs.title: Every Hour
songs.modern_archetype: Empowered pop-rock act-one-finale anthem: the heroine decides alone to keep going while everyone around her freezes, ending in a stacked multi-voice cliffhanger
songs.production_dna: Driving pop-rock act-one finale, 132 BPM, pulsing eighth-note piano and palm-muted electric guitars, big live drums, synth arpeggios and soaring strings, ensemble chant, TAP (crisp double tick of rimshot and glockenspiel) on the counts, GLIDE (harp-and-synth shimmer into legato strings) while things go well, a sudden full-band hit and a straining string glissando for the near-tear, a half-time night section of quick alternating solo lines over a low synth pulse, dry close-miked voices from above, a hush into the SCARLETT signature (sliding sub-bass, muted trumpet, finger snaps), then a key change into a huge sustained mezzo belt over stacked call-and-echo chorus, a cliffhanger chord and an abrupt cut. British English diction.
songs.structure:
Key change: the final chorus, where Prox belts over everyone.

[Intro | ENSEMBLE, driving piano] Time stamp: 'Day ten. The skin stitches came out today. / The tendon ones never will.'

[Verse 1 | PROX, hopeful] 'straight inside the splint and never past it'.

songs.hook_idea: Prox's specific, unpreachy power anthem is about counting reps when no one else will: 'If you won't pull, and he won't move, / then I'll count for both of us. / Every hour! songs.hook_idea: The opener's chant comes back as an earned, relaxed singalong: 'We've got it in hand! (Got it in hand!) / The coffee, the keys, the lunchbox and Wren!' The meaning has flipped from control to letting go, and no one says so. The show's last words are still the bible's 'Make a fist for me. / Now open.'
